title: Properties of Operations: Commutative, Associative and Distributive
seo_title: Grade 4 Properties of Operations Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Recognise and use the commutative, associative and distributive properties with whole numbers.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 worksheets on properties of operations: commutative, associative and distributive properties and 0 and 1. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Order and grouping do not change + and ×.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Commutative: the order does not change the answer for + and ×: 7 + 5 = 5 + 7; 4 × 9 = 9 × 4.
  • Associative: the grouping does not change the answer for + and ×: (2 × 5) × 7 = 2 × (5 × 7).
  • Distributive: 6 × 14 = 6 × 10 + 6 × 4.
  • Subtraction and division are not commutative.

Examples

Example

8 × 23

8 × 20 + 8 × 3

160 + 24

Answer: 184

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Subtraction turned around9 − 4 ≠ 4 − 9.
Multiplying one partMultiply every part.
× 0Any number × 0 = 0.

items.q: The pans balance, so 45 + 38 = 40 + ?. What is the missing number?
items.e: = means both sides have the same value. The left side is 45 + 38 = 83. So 40 + ? = 83 and ? = 43. Or: 40 is 5 less than 45, so ? must be 5 more than 38. Not 83: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 33: that changes 38 the wrong way.

items.q: The pans balance, so 27 + 56 = 30 + ?. What is the missing number?
items.e: = means both sides have the same value. The left side is 27 + 56 = 83. So 30 + ? = 83 and ? = 53. Or: 30 is 3 more than 27, so ? must be 3 less than 56. Not 83: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 59: that changes 56 the wrong way.

= means both sides have the same value. The left side is 68 + 25 = 93. So 70 + ? = 93 and ? = 23. Or: 70 is 2 more than 68, so ? must be 2 less than 25. Not 93: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 27: that changes 25 the wrong way.

= means both sides have the same value. The left side is 134 + 58 = 192. So 130 + ? = 192 and ? = 62. Or: 130 is 4 less than 134, so ? must be 4 more than 58. Not 192: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 54: that changes 58 the wrong way.

= means both sides have the same value. The left side is 246 + 97 = 343. So 250 + ? = 343 and ? = 93. Or: 250 is 4 more than 246, so ? must be 4 less than 97. Not 343: that is the value of the left side, not the missing number. Not 101: that changes 97 the wrong way.
You can add in any order: 245 + 38 = 38 + 245. So ? = 245. Not 283: = means “the same as”, so ? is not the answer to 245 + 38.
Turn-around facts: 167 + 59 = 59 + 167. So ? = 59. Not 226: that is the total of the left side.
You can add in any order, so 64 + 29 = 29 + 64 is true. You cannot subtract in any order: 64 − 29 = 35, but 29 − 64 does not give 35.
Subtraction does not work in any order. 50 − 20 = 30, but 20 − 50 is not 30. So 50 − 20 = 20 − 50 is not true.

items.q: Which number sentence has the same total as 36 + 47?
items.e: Changing the order of two numbers you add does not change the total: 36 + 47 = 47 + 36 = 83. 36 + 74 uses a different number (74, not 47).

items.q: Lerato says 85 − 40 = 40 − 85, because you can add in any order. What is wrong?
c: Addition cannot be done in any order
Subtraction cannot be done in any order
items.e: The turn-around rule works for addition only. 85 − 40 = 45, but 40 − 85 is not 45. Subtraction cannot be done in any order.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
4 × 7 = 7 × 4
items.e: This is the commutative property. The factors switch places, and the product stays the same.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
(2 × 3) × 4 = 2 × (3 × 4)
items.e: This is the associative property. The factors stay in the same order. Only the parentheses move, which changes what you multiply first.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
6 × (5 + 2) = (6 × 5) + (6 × 2)
items.e: This is the distributive property. One factor is split into two parts. Each part is multiplied, and the products are added.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
9 × 1 = 9
items.e: This is the identity property of multiplication. Multiplying by 1 keeps the number the same.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
0 × 8 = 0
items.e: This is the zero property of multiplication. Multiplying by 0 always gives 0.

items.q:
Which property does this equation show?
(4 × 5) + (4 × 3) = 4 × 8
items.e: This is the distributive property. One factor is split into two parts. Each part is multiplied, and the products are added.

items.q: Which equation shows the commutative property?
items.e: Commutative means the order changes: 3 × 8 and 8 × 3 have the same factors in a different order.

items.q: Which equation shows the distributive property?
items.e: 6 is split into 5 + 1. Each part is multiplied by 7, and the two products are added: 35 + 7 = 42.

items.q: Lerato sets up 6 rows of 8 chairs. Sibusiso sets up 8 rows of 6 chairs. Who sets up more chairs?
items.e: 6 × 8 = 48 and 8 × 6 = 48, so they set up the same number. Switching the order does not change the product. (14 comes from adding 6 + 8.)

items.q: A box has 4 rows of 9 crayons. Lerato says the total is 4 × 9. Ethan says it is 9 × 4. Who is right?
items.e: 4 rows of 9 can also be read as 9 columns of 4. 4 × 9 = 9 × 4 = 36.
